newsitem.title: USA: Maine voters favor King's clear-cutting pact - poll.
newsitem.headline: Maine voters favor King's clear-cutting pact - poll.

text.p: Gov. Angus King's compromise measure, which would limit the clear-cutting of timber to 75 acre swaths, was supported by thirty-six percent of those surveyed in a poll that was conducted last week.

The telephone survey by Strategic Marketing Services found that 17 percent back a proposal advanced by the Green Party, which would ban the practice entirely, while 18 percent oppose both of the plans.
The current law allows paper companies to clear-cut tracts as large as 250 acres.
Around 30 percent of Maine's voters, who on November 5 will get to approve or reject both proposals, still are undecided, said Strategic Marketing.
